testResults.name: dev-parameter-file
testResults.result: The westus2 dev parameter file compiled; it contains no secret values and visibly selects the dev names, image digest sentinel, disabled external API ingress, and explicit Key Vault public-network choice. The composition explicitly keeps shared Log Analytics public query access disabled to match cost-controls.

testResults.name: compiled-composition-assertions
testResults.command: PowerShell static assertions over az bicep build --stdout compiled ARM JSON
testResults.result: Compiled ARM assertions found six resource-group modules for storage, identities, Key Vault, access, Container Apps, and cost controls; deterministic resource-group-derived naming; runtime identity resource and client ID wired to both workloads; runtime storage and Key Vault role-assignment inputs wired from module outputs; digest-addressed shared image input; explicit Key Vault network selection; shared Log Analytics workspace sequencing; 40 USD and 70 USD monthly budget controls; and the configured non-secret runtime guardrails

testResults.name: secret-free-and-deployment-boundary
testResults.result: The composition creates no Key Vault secrets and accepts no provider credentials, tokens, account keys, passwords, or registry credentials. The dev file contains only a fake digest-shaped image sentinel and REPLACE_WITH_BUDGET_CONTACT_EMAIL sentinel, both documented as mandatory user input before Azure operations

parametersRequiringUserInputBeforeAzure.requiredValue: The actual digest-addressed reference emitted by the GitHub GHCR publication workflow
A valid Cost Management notification email address
The first day of the intended monthly budget period when deployment occurs

limitations: No Azure login, az what-if, deployment, Cost Management operation, registry operation, or data-plane call was run by this validation.

The effective shared Log Analytics workspace retention is 30 days because the existing Container Apps module declares that workspace at 30 days; cost-controls receives the same value to keep the repeated resource declaration consistent.

The dev Key Vault public endpoint choice is enabled explicitly because no private endpoint or private DNS module is in scope. Key Vault remains Entra-only and RBAC-authorized; set allowPublicNetworkAccess to false only after private connectivity is composed.

A deployment still needs an Azure subscription, a westus2-capable resource group, and an authenticated Azure caller or the later GitHub OIDC workflow. No Bicep parameter contains a secret; any provider/API credentials must be seeded separately in Key Vault by an authorized process.
blockers: Azure what-if and deployment are intentionally deferred until the user supplies the actual GHCR digest, valid budget contact, deployment subscription/resource group context, and the approved Key Vault network posture.
